title: ITD District 2 Laboratory Heating Upgrades Rebid
scope: Complete ground truth for all nine supplied pages of the ITD District 2 heating-system-upgrades rebid set: project/sheet/scale review, every M3.0 schedule row and cell, schedule/plan reconciliation, printed control interface rows, network/control context, the written grey existing and bold updated sequence layers, and sensor/valve/actuator source limits. No unprinted installed I/O, controller, valve, damper-actuator, or zone-sensor quantity is invented.
reading_notes: The retained corpus has all nine pages of this supplied drawing set. Full-page Poppler renders establish page-level visual context; MuPDF and Poppler independently corroborate every authored schedule cell and bounded controls/reconciliation assertion.

M3.0 has 4 schedule tables / 11 line items: 1 existing AHU, 2 existing boilers, 6 new hydronic pumps, and 2 new VFDs. A schedule row is not automatically an installed drawing count; the 11 identities are separately anchored to plan/schematic context.

M4.0 and M4.1 explicitly say grey is existing control sequence and bold is updated control sequence. This record preserves both layers; it does not manufacture an integrated final control narrative where the source does not do so.

The only printed VFD and chiller points lists are open-ended interface lists. Their 16 visible source rows lack per-row AI/AO/DI/DO classifications and physical owner/multiplier data, so they are neither retyped nor inflated into a terminal count.

Legends, schematic transmitter/symbol marks, detail callouts, plan symbols, schedules and physical installed devices are distinct source constructs. Their quantities are retained only where the drawing set actually establishes them.

requirement_audit.finding: Project name, location, building description, agency, engineering firm, project number, rebid issue and issue date are captured; blank revision grids are not reclassified as revisions.

Every supplied sheet has a page-level sheet/title/review ledger. Sheet-ID/name lettering is visually legible outlined title-block graphics, so the source limitation is retained rather than asserting a false text-extraction witness.
The two M1.0 and two E1.0 plan views state 1/4" = 1'-0"; detail/controls/schedule pages are not distance-scaled plan views and no supplied page has a graphic scale bar.
All 11 M3.0 marked schedule identities are classified and reconciled to plan/schematic visual context. The BP-2 area-served source conflict remains explicit rather than corrected by assumption.
All four M3.0 schedules are retained as 11 exact source rows and 160 two-engine-corrobated cells, including airflow, capacity, flow, electrical, pump, VFD and selection fields.

Every visible row in the 4-row VFD and 12-row chiller interface lists is retained with its source scope. The lists are expressly open-ended and untyped, so no unsupported I/O-type or physical-terminal count is claimed.
Existing Delta system, BACnet, existing controller/operator components and explicitly absent transport/addressing/baud/controller-model information are recorded exactly at source scope.

M4.0 heating-water and M4.1 chilled-water written sequences are separated into existing-grey and updated-bold layers, with the VFD/chiller lists, key reset, delay, lead/lag, alarm, valve, UCP and diagram context retained.
Schematic/integration logical sensor roles are indexed. The supplied set does not map space, CO2 or smart-thermostat devices to zones, so physical counts remain explicitly not stated.

No valve/actuator schedules, no zone sensor roster, open-ended interface lists, outlined sheet-ID text, grey/bold layering, schedule-versus-installed distinctions and the BP-2 wording conflict are all explicitly recorded.
All nine supplied pages were reviewed at full-page resolution; the saved Poppler renders and each sheet finding are embedded and hash-checked in the final record.
Build and validation rerun every module against the retained MuPDF and Poppler source captures. The final record stores component and bundle digests in addition to the evidence source hash.

sequences.title: EXISTING HEATING WATER SYSTEM SEQUENCE OF OPERATION

statements.text: THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED WHENEVER BOTH OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITION EXISTS: OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE DECREASES TO THE HEATING ENABLE SET POINT FOR 10 CONSECUTIVE MINUTES; THERE IS A CALL FOR HEAT FROM AT LEAST ONE ZONE BASED ON A HEATING COIL CONTROL VALVE MINIMUM POSITION OF 25% OPEN FOR 30 CONSECUTIVE SECONDS.

SEND AN ENABLE COMMAND TO THE LEAD HEATING WATER PUMP; validate running status through the VFD control interface; enable the standby pump on a lead-pump failure and alarm if the standby pump fails to start.

THE DDC CONTROLLER SHALL MODULATE THE VFD BASED ON A DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SETPOINT (ADJUSTABLE) LOCATED ACROSS THE PIPING ASSEMBLY; the setpoint is coordinated between balance and control contractors and must allow adequate flow to all hot-water heating coils.
SEND AN ENABLE COMMAND TO THE BOILER SYSTEM'S UNIT CONTROLLER; validate through the UCP; on lead-boiler failure enable the lag boiler; alarm if either boiler fails to start.

DDC lead/lag control of heating-water pumps includes monthly lead rotation, manual/operator overrides, and lockout prevention: minimum 10 minutes run and 5 minutes off before restart except for manual or occupied/unoccupied scheduling control.
THE HEATING ENABLE SET POINT SHALL BE SET AT 60°F.

sequences.title: UPDATED CONTROL SEQUENCES ON EXISTING HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHEET

statements.text: EACH BOILER SHALL DISABLE ITS OWN BOILER PUMP RESPECTIVELY.
THE BYPASS CONTROL VALVE (BCV-1) SHALL BE DISABLE AND LOCKED OUT.

EACH BOILER SHALL ENABLE THE RESPECTIVE BOILER PUMP BEFORE FIRING THE BOILER. IF EITHER BOILER PUMP FAILS TO START, THE RESPECTIVE BOILER SHALL NOT ENABLE AND AN ALARM OF THE EVENT SHALL BE SENT TO THE OPERATOR'S WORKSTATION.

WHEN A RUNNING STATUS FROM THE BOILER UNIT CONTROL PANEL (UCP) HAS BEEN CONFIRMED, THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHALL CONTINUE TO OPERATE UNDER ITS OWN INTERNAL CONTROLS BY PROVIDING LEAD / LAG SEQUENCING AND ADJUSTING THEIR OWN RAMPING AND LOADING RATES. THE DDC CONTROLLER SHALL SEND THE UNIT CONTROL PANEL A HEATING WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SET POINT TO MAINTAIN.

Heating-water supply temperature reset is based on heating-coil-control-valve positions: first enabled maximum 140°F +/- 1°F, decreasing linearly to 100°F while all heating-coil control valves are 90% open or less; it reverses toward maximum when three or more are over 90%, and resets to maximum if one or more reach 100% for 60 consecutive seconds. All stated values are adjustable where printed.

sequences.title: EXISTING CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SEQUENCE OF OPERATION

statements.text: THE CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED WHENEVER ONE OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS EXIST: outside-air temperature rises to the cooling enable set point for 10 consecutive minutes; buffer-tank temperature rises above 45°F for 30 seconds; or there is a call for dehumidification.

SEND AN ENABLE COMMAND TO THE AIR-COOLED CHILLER'S UNIT CONTROL PANEL (UCP), validate chiller running status through the UCP, alarm on a failed start, and provide the UCP a chilled-water supply-temperature set point after confirmation.

THE CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE DISABLED WHENEVER BOTH OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS EXIST: outside-air temperature decreases 2° (adjustable) or more below the cooling-enable set point for 10 consecutive minutes (adjustable), and buffer-tank temperature falls below 45°F for 30 seconds.

DDC lead/standby primary-pump control provides automatic rotation by runtime, fixed rotation, or calendar date with manual/operator override. Cooldown disables the chilled-water system 10 minutes before occupied-to-unoccupied switchover of the last air-valve system to use residual cooling capacity in the piping system.
CHILLED WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SET POINT RESET is based on outdoor-air temperature: 60°F outdoor / 55°F supply and 75°F outdoor / 45°F supply, as printed.

sequences.title: UPDATED CONTROL SEQUENCES ON EXISTING CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SHEET

statements.text: SEND AN ENABLE COMMAND TO THE LEAD CHILLED WATER PUMP; validate running status through the current sensing relay; if the lead pump fails to start, enable the standby pump; if the standby pump fails to start, alarm the operator's workstation.

SEND A DISABLE COMMAND TO THE LEAD CHILLED WATER PUMP. When the chilled-water system is disabled, the lead primary chilled-water pump continues for 10 consecutive minutes; validate running status through the current sensing relay and alarm if the pump fails to stop.

supporting_evidence.module_role: Coordinator limitation ledger for the complete nine-page supplied ITD District 2 heating-upgrades rebid PDF. These source limits are findings from complete visual review, not parser absence claims alone.

source_limitations.finding: The title-block sheet IDs/names are legible on the full-page renders but largely outlined graphics rather than normal parser text. Visual review records them; no false parser assertion is made for those outlined labels.
No dedicated control-valve schedule appears on the nine supplied sheets. A new AHU-1 3-way-valve note, schematic BCV-1 label, and legend symbols are not converted to a valve-schedule count.
No dedicated damper-actuator schedule appears on the nine supplied sheets. The controls legend's DA definition is not an installed actuator quantity.
The VFD list says NOT BE LIMITED TO and the chiller list says ALL AVAILABLE and NOT BE LIMITED TO. The visible 16 rows are preserved but are not treated as a complete physical I/O count.

The supplied floor/power plans do not provide a space-sensor, CO2-sensor, or smart-thermostat roster mapped to zones. Schematic TT/PT and integration temperature points are recorded only as logical/source items.
M4.0/M4.1 explicitly label grey text as existing sequence and bold text as updated sequence. The two layers are preserved separately; the record does not invent a merged final sequence.
M3.0 has 11 schedule line items. Schedule rows, plan/schematic visual labels, logical source-list rows, and field-installed devices are different quantities and remain separately scoped.
